title: The month of Maghar
hook: in Maghar lovely are those who sit with the Beloved (Barah Maha, ang 135)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Katak: we earn what our deeds earn, and no one else is to blame. Today the week ends sitting down together.

Some good hours happen with nothing going on. A kitchen late at night, two people with tea, the dishes not done. A hospital waiting room where a friend just sits beside you and doesn't try to say anything wise. A grandparent on a bench, holding a small hand, watching pigeons. None of it would make a highlight reel, but these can be the moments that stay. Maghar, roughly mid-November to mid-December, is when the Punjabi cold comes in and people pull their chairs closer. Guru Arjan's Maghar stanza is about exactly that: sitting with.
screen: `TEA AT A LATE KITCHEN TABLE.` → `A FRIEND IN THE WAITING ROOM.` → `MAGHAR: SITTING WITH.`

segments.voice: The stanza opens, in paraphrase: in Maghar, lovely are those who sit with the Beloved, the Lord. Sohandee-aa, lovely, shining. Baithrree-aah, those who sit. That's all they're doing: not climbing, earning or proving, just seated beside the One they love, and the stanza says their beauty can't even be counted. Then the other side. Those who don't sit in the company of the holy stay alone. Their pain doesn't leave them, and they fall into death's grip. A whole Sikh practice lives inside that picture. In the diwan hall of a gurdwara, people take off their shoes, cover their heads, bow, and then sit on the floor, together, at the same level. Nobody has a better chair. They sit while the hymns are sung, sometimes a long time, sometimes saying nothing at all. That's sangat, the holy company, and in the Barah Maha it's where the bride finds the Beloved's presence. Look back over the week and you can see the road. In Jeth she bowed. In Asarh she learned to keep Him near in the heat. In Sawan she blossomed, in Bhadon she doubted, in Assu she longed and asked how, in Katak she stopped blaming. Now, in Maghar, she simply sits. The stanza ends: in Maghar, those who worship the Lord are not born again into the round of coming and going. The long journey of the months arrives somewhere very still.
screen: `SOHANDEE-AA: LOVELY ARE THOSE WHO SIT.` · `APART FROM THE HOLY, WE STAY ALONE.` · `SANGAT: SEATED ON ONE FLOOR.` · `THE WEEK'S ROAD ARRIVES IN STILLNESS.` · then, large: `MAGHAR: SIT TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: If someone you love is near, sit beside them now, no phone, no agenda; if not, bring one person to mind and sit as if they were next to you, their face, their hands, the way they settle into a chair. Don't plan a conversation; just be with. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru between breaths, the One the stanza calls the Beloved.
Maghar. In the Barah Maha, Maghar is the month of sitting: lovely are those who sit with the Beloved, and the holy company is where we sit.
Your line: maghar: sit together. Tea counts; a bench counts. Day five hundred seventy-four, done.

howItsDone: In the gurdwara, Sikhs sit together on the floor of the diwan hall, at one level, to hear kirtan; on the Sangrand of Maghar gurdwaras that keep the day read Guru Arjan's Maghar stanza from the Barah Maha.

original.note: Gurmukhi: sangat, the company, the congregation that sits together to sing and listen.

trapdoor: what you thought: Maghar is a cold month, so the stanza is about weather.
what it means: it's about the beauty of simply sitting with the Beloved, in holy company.
what a scholar hears: the stanza promises that those who worship the Lord in Maghar are not born again, placing the end of the cycle of births in an act as plain as sitting.

chat.says: Isn't faith mostly about doing things? Why praise people who just sit?
options: The Maghar stanza calls lovely those who sit with the Beloved; in sangat, sitting together is the practice.
The Maghar stanza praises sitting only because winter is too cold for useful work to be done.
The Maghar stanza means sitting alone in silence, since company only distracts from the Beloved.
chat.meaning: In Maghar, lovely are those who sit with the Beloved; those who don't sit in holy company stay alone, and their pain doesn't leave.

Maghar.meaning: mid-November to mid-December, when the cold comes

diwan.meaning: the gurdwara hall where the sangat sits together
